english: A man who was leading ten sheep came to the house. The master of the house was standing at the door. [The man said:] "Give me your daughter." [The master:] "What is the bride price?" [The man:] "The bride price is so many (this many)." Then the master gave him his own daughter. They drank and they rejoiced.
uncertain: wédʰet: PST.3SG of 'lead' (or homonym 'bind/marry'); read 'was leading (the sheep)'
dʰugh₂térm̥ moy toy: moy/toy are each GEN or DAT enclitic; read moy DAT 'to me', toy GEN 'your'
tóti: 'so many', presumably pointing at the ten sheep
h₁opéyet: PST 'was giving', read as narrative 'gave'

english: "Mother, where is father?" "He is in the cow-stall." "Give me something to drink." "Son, drink." "What are you weaving?" "I am weaving wool." "I saw a wolf." "Where did you see it?" "I saw it at the door." "Do not be afraid of it. Sit down."
uncertain: srobʰéye me: causative 'make me sip' = 'give me a drink' (or 'let me suck/nurse')
wébʰesi/wébʰoh₂: indicative present or subjunctive; read as present
speaker turns are inferred; who says 'I saw a wolf' (the son?) is not marked
kʷéḱs: AOR.2SG of 'see' (also matches another stem as PST/IMP)

english: Lead the two cattle (oxen) out of the cow-stall. Then yoke the two to the plough. Do not beat them. Drive them with your voice (with a word). When the two grow tired, let them lie down (rest). Then drive them into the cow-stall.
uncertain: tóh₁: masc NOM/ACC dual or INS.SG; read ACC.DU 'the two (oxen)' throughout
ḱémh₂etes: SBJV 2DU or 3DU; read 3DU 'they (two) grow tired'
logʰéye: causative 'make lie down', i.e. let them rest

english: When a guest stands at the door, stand up and go to the door. Lead him into the house. Give him grain (wheat). Seat him at the table (on the seat). Do not kill him: he is dear to the god. When day dawns (or: when he has stayed the night), let him go.
uncertain: gʰóstis: 'guest' or 'stranger/enemy'; the ban on killing suggests both senses are in play
stóloy: LOC of 'seat/table/equipment'
h₂wéseti: PRS.3SG 'stays/dwells (overnight)' or SBJV.3SG 'becomes bright at dawn'; tód as neuter subject makes 'when it dawns' likelier, but ambiguous
l̥h₁dʰí: 'let go, allow'; read 'let him go'
puHróm: a kind of grain, maybe wheat/spelt

english: The horse(s) said: "Listen, sheep! The heart is pained for us seeing [this]: man, the master, makes the sheep's wool into a warm garment for himself; and the sheep have no wool."
uncertain: (h₁)éḱwōs: NOM.PL 'horses' (also VOC.PL); parentheses mark an optional laryngeal
ewewkʷ: not analyzed; looks like a reduplicated/augmented 3SG past of wekʷ- 'speak' = 'said'
h₂gʰnutoy: not analyzed; read as middle 3SG 'is pained/grieves'
widntbʰós: not analyzed; read DAT.PL participle 'to (us) seeing'
dʰǵʰémō(n): not in lexicon; read 'man, earthling'
h₂wlnéh₂m / h₂wlh₂néh₂: not analyzed; spelling variants of 'wool' (ACC / NOM)
h₂ówyom: the analyzer matches only 'egg' (NOM/ACC/GEN.PL); context needs 'of sheep' (GEN.PL) or 'ovine'
kʷnewti: not analyzed; read as 'makes' (kʷr̥néwti without the r̥)
sébʰoy: not analyzed; read reflexive dative 'for himself'
gʷʰérmom: not analyzed; read 'warm'
wéstrom: lexicon gives no gloss; root 'dress, clothe', so 'garment'
h₂éwibʰoskʷe: DAT/ABL.PL 'sheep' + -kʷe; dative of possession 'the sheep have no wool'
misfit: ewewkʷ: not analyzed, but looks like a 3SG past ('said'), while its subject h₁éḱwōs is NOM.PL 'horses'; a number mismatch (the item uses a different notation, so this may just be the notation)

english: Wake up at dawn. Then drive the flock out, and take the dog along with you. Do not lie down. Watch it (the flock) and listen to him (the dog). If the wolf comes, cry out. Strike him with the spear. Then drive the flock into the enclosure (fold). Father Dyeus, may you protect it.
uncertain: tód ... tóm-kʷe: neuter tód fits h₂éǵmn̥ (neuter 'flock'); masc tóm read as the dog, but it could be the wolf or the flock loosely
wéh₁ikom: lexicon 'enclosed' (adj.); read as substantive 'the enclosure, fold' (goal accusative)
h₂éǵmn̥: 'flock' (also 'army, crowd')
gʷréwh₁: INS 'with the spear' (or 'spit')

english: A brother and a sister went to the water, and it was deep. Fish were swimming in it. Then the brother struck (killed) a fish with a spear. Then the sister cooked it. Then the two of them ate, and they were satisfied. Then the two sat (resting).
uncertain: h₁r̥sḱétām: PST.3DU or IMP.3DU 'go to, arrive'; read narrative 3DU
h₁ést: PST.3SG 'was' (also AOR 'threw'); read 'was'
sn̥h₂ént: PST.3PL 'were swimming' or AOR.3PL 'caught'; swimming fits the fish as subject
gʷʰént: PST 'was striking/killing'; read 'struck'
h₁dtā́m: 3DU of 'eat'
misfit: tóy-kʷe tetr̥pḗr: NOM.PL pronoun and PRF.3PL for the same two siblings who take dual everywhere else (h₁r̥sḱétām, tóh₁ h₁dtā́m, tóh₁ sísdetām); expected dual. Plural for two is possible, but odd in this text

english: "Brother, what is fame?" "It is a famous name." "Who has fame (to whom is fame)?" "Whoever kills a bear, great fame is his." "Did you kill a bear?" "They killed it (?), and my name is famous." "May my name be famous."
uncertain: ḱlutóm: adj. 'famous' (NOM/ACC.SG neut.); also matches AOR/IMP.2DU 'hear', which does not fit
gʷʰénti h₁ésti: relative clause 'who kills' followed by 'is (great fame to him)'
gʷʰéns: PST.2SG 'were you killing / did you kill'
the final wish 'may my name be famous' clashes with the previous 'my name is famous'; speaker split is unclear
misfit: gʷʰnént: PST.3PL 'they killed', but the reply to 'did you kill a bear?' together with 'my name is famous' needs 1SG 'I killed it'

english: "Dear friend, where is the flock?" "It is under the tree." "Have you seen the wolf?" "I have seen him in front of the enclosure." "Let us guard the flock. You go with the dog. I am going over there (to the other side). Father Dyeus, protect us."
uncertain: ḱéywe: VOC.SG of ḱéywos 'dear, intimate'; also matches PST.1DU 'we two were lying', which does not fit
h₂énti: LOC 'in front (of)', or particle
wéh₁ikoy: LOC of 'enclosed' (adj.) read as 'enclosure'
h₂én: 'there, yonder, on the other side'

english: The mother took the wool and spun (twisted) it. She sat at the door. Then, stretching the wool, she wove (it). When dawn broke, she clothed her son with it. He rejoiced.
uncertain: uh₁inéHt: lexicon has no gloss; root 'twist, wind, weave', so 'spun/twisted'
tékst: lexicon has no gloss; root 'weave'
séh₂: fem. NOM 'she' (also matches IMP 'become sated', which does not fit)
h₂wést: AOR 'became bright (at dawn)'; also PST of 'dwell'
téh₂eh₁: fem. INS 'with it' = the wool

english: [Let the two of them] go to the enclosure at dawn. Then sit with the sheep. Do not cry out. Do not push (hit) them. Speak to them. Milk them. Carry the load inside.
uncertain: wéh₁ikom: 'enclosed' (adj.) read as 'enclosure' (goal)
bʰh₂dʰí: 'speak' (homonym 'shine' does not fit)
h₂ówins/tā́s: sheep treated as feminine
misfit: gʷh₂tā́m: 3DU (AOR 'the two went' or IMP 'let the two go') with no dual subject, in a run of 2SG commands; expected 2SG gʷh₂dʰí 'go'

english: The Sheep and the Horses.
uncertain: owis, eḱwōs: not analyzed; old spelling without laryngeals (h₂ówis 'sheep', h₁éḱwōs 'horses' NOM.PL)
kʷe: written as a separate word; read as enclitic -kʷe 'and'
a title; no verb

english: The grain grew (ripened). Then father and mother went to the field. He cut the ears of grain, and she carried the load. The two sons dried the ears. Then they put the load on the wagon, and two swift horses pulled it. Then she cooked (or ground) the grain. Then, eating it, they rejoiced. "Mother Earth, you gave us grain."
uncertain: h₂éḱōs: NOM/ACC.PL 'ears of grain' (also 'sharpness')
pékʷyet: lexicon has no gloss; root 'crack, crush (grain), cook', so 'ground' or 'cooked/baked'
dʰh₁ént: AOR.3PL 'they put'; subject is unstated (the family)
tóm: masc ACC = the load (or the wagon)
kʷékʷloy: LOC 'on the wagon/cart'
h₂sowséyetām: PST/IMP 3DU; read narrative 'the two dried'
déh₃s: AOR.2SG 'you gave'

english: "Dear friend, have you seen the sheep?" "I have not seen her. She is gone." "Did the wolf take her?" "I do not know that. Let us search for her. Go to the cow-stall, and I will go to the door." ... "I found her under the tree." "Is she alive?" "She is alive."
uncertain: ḱéywe: VOC 'dear friend' (or PST.1DU 'lie', which does not fit)
séh₂: fem. 'she' (homonym IMP 'become sated' does not fit)
speaker turns are inferred

english: "Who is standing at the door?" "I am a thirsty guest. Give me something to drink." "Come in." "Are you the master of the house?" "I am the master. Sit down and eat grain."
uncertain: srobʰéye me: causative 'make me sip' = 'give me a drink'
speaker turns: the guest asks 'are you the master?'; read so
dʰh₁méns: GEN.SG 'of the house'

english: When it was getting dark, a stranger stole two horses. Then the man woke and did not see them. "Son, wake up!" "Who took them?" "That one (he) took them." Then the dog tracked them, and the man followed it. Then they found the two over there. He (the thief) was afraid and went away. Then he (the man) drove the two home.
uncertain: h₁regʷesyét: impersonal 'it was getting dark'
gʰóstis: 'stranger, enemy' here (also 'guest')
tóh₁: ACC.DU 'the two (horses)' throughout
widónt: AOR.3PL 'they found'; subject (man and dog/son) is unstated
só in 'dedwóyth₂e só': presumably the thief; the referent is unclear
léytt: 'went away' (homonym 'touch' does not fit with h₂epó)
misfit: dedwóyth₂e: PRF.2SG 'you are afraid' with 3SG subject só; expected 3SG dedwóye

english: Dawn shone. Then the man stood up and went to his field. Yoking two oxen to the plough, he drove them. Then he ploughed with the plough, and the sun was high. Sweating, he grew tired. Then he cried out to Dyeus (the sky): "Father Dyeus, give my field water (or: my father Dyeus, give water to the field)." Dyeus heard him, and it rained, and the cloud went away. When it was getting dark, he led the two home. Then he was asleep.
uncertain: moy: GEN 'my (father)' or DAT 'to me'
h₂wérst: AOR.3SG 'rained', impersonal or with Dyeus as subject
bʰérǵʰont: neut. 'high' agreeing with sóh₂wl̥ (also verb forms)
h₁ést: 'was' (homonym 'threw' does not fit)
diwéy: DAT 'to Dyeus/sky'

english: Cook (grind) the grain. Then bring fire into the house and put water on it. When it boils, put it (the grain) in it. Set up the table. Then sit at the table and eat the grain.
uncertain: pékʷye: lexicon has no gloss; root 'crack, crush grain, cook'
dʰéh₁mn̥: goal 'into the house' (could be the object of dʰh₁dʰí instead)
tósmi: LOC 'on/in it'; first = the fire, second = the water
tóm: masc = the grain (puHrós); tód neut. = the water
sísdete gʷr̥h₃éte: 2PL (IMP or PRS), a switch from 2SG commands to plural 'you all'
the order (cook first, then make the fire) is odd; the first line may be a heading

english: When it was getting dark, a wolf crept to the enclosure. The flock trembled. The dog heard it and howled (cried out). Then the man woke. Then, seizing his spear, he saw the wolf at the door. Then he killed it with that (spear). Then he lay down again.
uncertain: wéh₁ikom: 'enclosed' read as goal 'the enclosure'
tóh₁: INS.SG 'with it' (the spear); could also be ACC.DU, which does not fit
h₂ew: 'again' (or 'away')

english: A cloud appeared, and it rained. Then the sheep trembled. The man led them into the enclosure. The ram went in front, and they followed. Then he sat at the door. Then it grew bright (dawned/cleared), and they came out.
uncertain: trésont: PST.3PL 'trembled' (also participle)
pró: preverb 'forward, in front'
tód h₂wést: AOR 'became bright' with neuter tód (maybe the cloud, nébʰos, or 'it' = day); or PST of 'dwell/spend the night' ('that one stayed'). Ambiguous
h₁n̥dʰént: 'came forth'; subject = the sheep

english: "Did you make the spear?" "I made it. Look at it. It is long, and it is sharp." "What shall I give you?" "Give me grain." "I give grain in exchange. May it bring you good fame."
uncertain: wérǵs/wérǵm̥: homonyms 'work, make' / 'enclose' / 'shear'; 'make' fits
widé: IMP.2SG 'see' (or PRF.2PL 'you know')
piḱróm: 'pointed, sharp' (also 'bitter, variegated')
dédeh₃mi: PRS 'I give' used in a question, 'what am I to give you?'
h₂m̥bʰí: 'in exchange for'
h₁opéyoyh₁t: OPT 'may it make reach / grant'
misfit: h₁wésuh₂: NOM/ACC.PL 'good (things)' does not agree with singular ḱléwos (expected h₁wésu); or read 'good things and fame'

english: "Sister, is the fire burning?" "It is burning, and the water is boiling. Brother, cook the grain." "I am preparing it." "Who is eating the grain?" "The dog is eating it." "Do not hit him; he is dear."
uncertain: speaker turns are inferred
ǵr̥h₂nóm / puHróm: two different 'grain' words

english: When dawn shone, the man led the cattle out of the cow-stall. Then they went to the field. They ate and they drank. When the sun was high, he sat under the tree. When it was getting dark, he drove them into the cow-stall. Then he was asleep, and the dog guarded them.
uncertain: h₁dént: AOR.3PL 'ate' (or PST)
bʰérǵʰont: neut. 'high'
h₁ést: 'was'
misfit: h₂éwsos: VOC.SG (or GEN of 'ear'), but it is the subject of léwkt; expected NOM h₂éwsōs

english: Take the wool from the ram. Dry it. Then spin (twist) it and stretch it. Do not break it. Plait (weave) it. Clothe yourself with it. May the wool warm you.
uncertain: uh₁inHdʰí: lexicon has no gloss; root 'twist, wind', so 'spin'
pléḱte: lexicon has no gloss; root 'fold, plait, weave'
h₁pdʰí: 'grasp, seize, take'
moysṓd: ABL 'from the ram' (or 'fleece')
gʷʰr̥nuyéh₁t: OPT 'may it warm/heat'

english: The daughter was working in the field. Then a bear came out from the trees. She was afraid and cried out. Her brother heard her, and seizing his spear, he came to her. The bear saw him and went away. Then she rejoiced.
uncertain: bʰebʰóyh₂e: PRF 1SG or 3SG; 3SG with séh₂
dréwbʰos: DAT/ABL.PL; ablative 'from the trees'
gʷémt + tā́m: 'came to her'

english: The man put the bronze (copper) into the fire. Then the bronze melted. Then, grasping it, he hammered (beat) it. He made a spear, and it was sharp. Then a stranger (guest) came and bought it. He gave grain in exchange.
uncertain: h₂éyos: 'copper, bronze, metal'
tinéh₁t: 'melted' (also 'became moist / finished cooking')
stunédt: 'was beating, pushing'; hammering fits
gʰóstis: 'guest' or 'stranger'
wérǵt: 'made' (homonyms 'enclose', 'shear')

english: "Where are you going?" "I am going to the king's house." "What are you carrying?" "I am carrying wool. The way is long; let us talk together." "Who is the king (what is he like)?" "The king has great fame, and his name is famous."
uncertain: bʰéh₂omes: SBJV.1PL 'let us speak' (homonym 'shine' does not fit); ḱóm 'together'
h₃rēǵéy h₁ésti: dative of possession 'to the king is great fame'
ḱlutóm: adj. 'famous'
speaker turns are inferred

english: Having heard that, the sheep fled to the field (plain).
uncertain: ḱeḱlōts, owis, aǵrom, ebʰuget: not analyzed; old spelling without laryngeals
ḱeḱlōts: read as perfect active participle of ḱlew- 'hear'
owis: 'sheep' NOM.SG
aǵrom: 'field' ACC (goal)
ebʰuget: read as augmented 3SG past of bʰewg- 'flee'
